text: Xylem is a leading global water technology company. We design, manufacture and service products and solutions that move, treat, analyse and return water to the environment, and we provide software and services that help utilities and industrial customers manage water networks. We operate through four segments: Water Infrastructure, Applied Water, Measurement and Control Solutions, and Water Solutions and Services. Our products include pumps, valves, mixers, disinfection systems, smart meters and leak-detection networks, and are sold in more than 150 countries. Approximately 95% of our revenue is derived from products and services that contribute to clean water access, water quality, water efficiency or resilience to drought and flooding. We do not manufacture tobacco, alcohol, weapons or fossil fuel extraction equipment, and we do not operate in the oil and gas exploration and production market.

Our results depend on capital spending by public water utilities, which is funded by rates and by government programmes and can be deferred during periods of fiscal pressure. A reduction in infrastructure funding, or delays in the award of contracts under such programmes, could reduce our revenue growth. We are exposed to supply chain disruption for electronic components used in our metering products, to competition from lower-cost pump manufacturers in Asia, and to exchange rate movements, as roughly half of our revenue is denominated in currencies other than the US dollar. Our products are subject to drinking water safety and product certification regimes, and a failure to meet those standards could result in recalls or exclusion from tenders.

From time to time we are party to legal proceedings arising in the ordinary course of business, including contract disputes, employment claims and product warranty matters. We are also a defendant in asbestos-related claims arising from products manufactured by predecessor businesses decades ago; the number of pending claims has declined for five consecutive years and the Company's recorded liability for these matters was $18 million at December 31, 2025. We do not believe that any pending proceeding, individually or in the aggregate, will have a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations or cash flows. No environmental proceeding is pending to which a governmental authority is a party and in which monetary sanctions of $300,000 or more are expected.

Water regulators in England and Wales have set leakage reduction targets that will require companies to find and fix hundreds of thousands of hidden leaks over the next decade, work that depends on acoustic sensors, pressure monitoring and the analytics software that interprets them. Suppliers including Xylem and a handful of specialist rivals have signed multi-year framework agreements covering sensor supply and managed services. Analysts said the contracts are unusually long by industrial standards, which smooths revenue but also locks in pricing before inflation is known. Charities investing with an environmental mission have shown interest in the sector because the capital spending is mandated by regulators rather than discretionary.

Xylem said it won a seven-year contract with a US municipal utility to supply and operate advanced metering infrastructure for 740,000 service connections, including meters, the communications network and leak-detection analytics. The company did not disclose the contract value. Management said the award supports its target of mid-single-digit organic revenue growth and that backlog in its Measurement and Control Solutions segment reached a record at the end of the second quarter.
